page: Microsoft Azure E16-4ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, 128.0 GB of system memory, and a 614 GB local storage drive. The CPU cache configuration consists of 48 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache, with support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AES cryptography.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile characterized by moderate single-core capabilities but constrained multi-core and memory throughput. Single-core performance is average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1629.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1896.98. However, multi-core scaling is weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 3499.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 3868.76. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached read and write speeds of 28.87 GB/sec and 25.23 GB/sec respectively, which are categorized as weak. This indicates a tradeoff where the massive memory capacity is paired with relatively low processing throughput and memory bandwidth.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per core and the inclusion of 614 GB of local storage, this server is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring large memory footprints but low parallel processing demands. It is suitable for memory-intensive applications such as caching layers, small-to-medium database operations, and text processing tasks. However, it is poorly suited for compute-heavy parallel workloads, multi-threaded decompression, or high-throughput web serving due to its weak multi-core performance and restricted memory bandwidth.

Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, it includes 614 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage. While single-core benchmarks like Geekbench (1629.0) and stress-ng (1896.98) show average performance, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are weak, with uncached read bandwidth at 28.87 GB/sec. This hardware profile makes the server qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy, low-compute workloads such as caching, text processing, and small database operations, while presenting a clear tradeoff for parallel processing or high-throughput applications.
